correctness.rationale: Squaring the central-binomial factor kills k of binary weight at least two modulo 16. At k=2^j the remaining Lucas bit is b_j xor b_(j+1), including zero for k>n. Thus A_n=1+4(n mod 2)+8r(n) mod 16. Appending 0 gives (0,u xor p,u); appending 1 gives (1,u,v xor (1-p)). I rebuilt the eight-state matrix, checked its characteristic polynomial x^3(x-2)(x-1)^2(x^2-2x+2) and the stated annihilator. The column and row sums give the constant dominant projection and the annihilator precludes loss of a polynomial factor at the other nonzero eigenvalues. A fixed prefix gives the same entrywise O(2^(L/2)) bound on every aligned block of length 2^L; geometric summation yields the all-cutoff error. The even word decodes its three bits, and for each parity of t the odd parameterization decodes the underlying three-bit state bijectively. Thus truncations at arbitrary N change counts by at most O(1) on splitting into the parity subclasses, giving 8/16 and 16/32 as the two contributions to total mass. For sharpness, the L=4,8,12 counts are 1,36,496; after four steps the surviving recurrence roots are 16,1,-4, giving the claimed sequence from m=1. An independent check of the identity is that s(t)=(0,0,0) iff t=4a with an even number of runs of 1s in a. For L=4m there are binom(L-1,2j) suffix strings with j such runs; filtering for j even gives 2^(L-3)+Re((1+i)^(L-1))/2. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_replay.py 1 independently checks direct binomial sums through n=179, 8,192 windows, the transfer polynomial, and the special state at four dyadic cutoffs. The finite data corroborate the proof; the frozen verifier was read, not run.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact local correlation law for the classical mod-16 Apéry sequence, not a selection of a few tested residues. It explains all eight extra exclusions beyond alternating mod-4 classes, quantifies the unequal frequencies of the permitted words, and supplies a concrete cell witnessing that all-cutoff square-root accuracy cannot be uniformly improved. These are more informative than the one-point congruence or mere automaton recognition; no claim is made for longer blocks or larger moduli.
